entries.notes: Both upward/downward collision branches accounted for; rounding discrepancy in supplement noted.

The displayed cot^3(alpha) relation is necessary, not by itself sufficient for flexible strings: tensile forces must be nonnegative; q=Q formally gives negative tension. Original physical model needs editorial clarification.
Airplane B flies EAST by SOUTH 30°, not SOUTH by EAST 30°; v_A/B magnitude about 916.5 km/h.
The 0.926 km/s day/night difference is conditional on equatorial alignment of the rotational surface velocity with the Earth orbital velocity; verify fig. 1.24 before releasing.
Source scan explicitly specifies theta=30 degrees; numeric tension/normal force and critical acceleration now evaluated at this angle.
Drawing board from under object requires relative slip; threshold differs from only overcoming table friction.

Book explicitly prints 38×10^5 km for ground control distance; retained as source text despite likely order-of-magnitude anomaly. Orbital result uses lunar radius, mass and 200 km altitude, not Earth-control distance.
Solar-Earth L1 and L2 approximate distance; rotation-frame assumptions explicit.
Book labels bottom pressure; computed force from hydrostatic pressure times bottom area, assumptions documented.
Critical theta=0 point needs quartic stability rather than second derivative test alone.
Moment flux force is calculated; pressure boundary conditions not provided for full bend load.

Source textbook fuel consumption 1.29×10^3 kg/s verified. Companion solution PDF page53 prints h=172 km, but independent analytic integration and numerical quadrature yield approximately 203.6 km with the book's assumptions; unresolved difference explicitly flagged.
Companion PDF page54 gives centroid 0.061a ABOVE cube center, equivalent to derived 0.561a ABOVE bottom; source fig 3.38 confirms cylindrical bore touches lower face.
Maximum charge error is 24×10^-21 e, not 24×10^-21 C; gravity dominates even worst-case electrostatic force.
Proof applies to the planar disk closing the hemisphere, not the hemispherical curved surface.
Uranium nucleus charge 92e; non-relativistic uniformly charged sphere model.
Textbook energy standard is table 4.1 on V1 PDF physical page131.
Original end-of-chapter 4.8 is vertical spring effective potential; do not confuse with 'thought question 4.8' on PDF p150.
Textbook energy standard is table 4.1 on V1 PDF physical page131.
Lightning energy is qU for constant average discharge potential; capacitive complete discharge from initial U gives 1/2 qU: not fully disambiguated by source.
Shell self-energy classical-electron radius differs by factor two from conventional definition; explicitly documented.
Source correctly states palladium nuclei with Z=46, not cesium Z=55.
